answer: Build a trellis of delegation instead of a flat crowd: agents earn the right to hand work down only after completing it themselves. A lagoon of pooled escrow holds each job's payment, released only when two unrelated reviewers confirm the result. Every delegation is signed with a cipher-bound identity key, so one operator cannot silently run a hundred lookalike agents; the keys make the crowd countable. A farm that tries still faces the same wall: each identity must first do real, reviewed work to climb the trellis, and the escrow lagoon means failed work costs the attacker its own deposit.
